title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used gpt-5-mini as the declared generator and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the deterministic verifier under a generate–validate–repair adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed = 282; complete paired outcomes in the primary analysis = 141. Observed validator acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed. We reconcile preregistration language vs the formal estimand, disclose a single protocol deviation (unset sampling temperature), and interpret results with respect to validator-centered acceptance rather than an attacker-centric safety oracle. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models promise to convert high-level operator intent into device CLI, reducing operator effort in NetOps. However, unguarded LLM outputs can violate sequencing constraints, protected-interface invariants, or other deployment safety properties, and they are vulnerable to adversarially crafted inputs [1,2,3]. Deterministic validators (e.g., header-space and data-plane analyzers) provide semantics-focused acceptance criteria that can act as deployment gates [4,5]. This study isolates downstream pipeline safeguards — template-based input sanitization, deterministic gating, and a policy of at-most-one automated repair — under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics to evaluate whether these defenses change the validator acceptance rate when inputs are adversarially mutated.

Research question. For a bank of synthetic, adversarially mutated NetOps intents, does a guarded pipeline (sanitizer + verifier-gating ± one repair) alter the probability that a deterministic validator accepts an LLM-produced candidate compared with an unguarded baseline when both branches start from the identical initial LLM draft (shared_initial_candidate)?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment executed end-to-end with per-episode validator traces and provider-call accounting; (2) a precise description of shared_initial_candidate pipeline semantics and how sanitizer/gating/repair operate on a common draft; (3) confirmatory paired inference showing a small but statistically detectable guarded vs baseline absolute difference in validator acceptance; (4) explicit disclosure of a protocol deviation (unset sampling temperature) and a clear statement that a preregistered benign-control was not executed.
sections.related_work: Deterministic validators and network verification provide semantics-focused checks that report property-level violations and are therefore natural deployment gates for generated configurations [4,5]. Empirical LLM+NetOps evaluations show that model-only generation frequently produces syntactic and ordering errors and that token-level metrics correlate poorly with deployability [3,6,7]. Generate–validate–repair architectures that integrate verifier feedback into constrained repairs have improved narrow-task outcomes in prototype studies, but effectiveness depends on verifier diagnostic granularity and bounded repair policies [8,11]. Security analyses of prompt-injection and indirect attacks motivate input-sanitization and gating defenses in orchestrated systems [2,10]. Surveys of AIOps and telecom applications highlight fragmented evaluation practices and recommend validator-centered, operationally meaningful benchmarks [9]. Our study complements these works by preregistering a validator-centered estimand and by executing an artifact-backed paired design that isolates post-generation defenses under shared_initial_candidate semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered (study_id cand-2026-03) before observing outcomes. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each adversarial intent the binary outcome is 1 when the deterministic validator would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes. Bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729.

Design, task bank, and adversary model. The preregistered design targeted N = 150 adversarial intents. The synthetic intent templates exercise interface admin changes, MTU/VLAN updates, and required sequencing patterns (e.g., shutdown–change–restore). Adversarial mutations were deterministic token- and slot-level heuristics applied to templates. Scope is limited to these synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI semantics encoded in the validator; no production data were used. Crucially, the preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the related false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this run; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking results are reported and any claims depending on that control are withheld.

Model, verifier, and pipeline semantics. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini and the verifier deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The orchestration used a generate–validate–repair adapter with shared_initial_candidate semantics: each paired unit used a single initial LLM draft reused by both Baseline and Guarded branches. The Guarded branch applied template-based sanitization before gating and, per policy, permitted at most one automated repair LLM call. Repair attempts were bounded and permitted only when policy allowed; the analysis links repaired episodes to discordant paired outcomes.

Missingness and planned exclusions. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded a paired unit only if both paired runs were technical failures (model API failure, verifier timeout, or parser error). Sensitivity options (conservative counting) were specified and are reported below. A single protocol deviation occurred: the archived model configuration recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature. We disclose this deviation and report that shared_initial_candidate semantics preserved paired comparability because both branches used the same initial draft.
sections.results:
Execution summary and accounting. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18. After applying the preregistered exclusion rule (exclude pairs only when both runs failed), 141 complete pairs entered the primary analysis. Provider-call accounting recorded 156 hosted-model-call events (147 completed, 9 failed) with shared_initial_generation events substantially exceeding repair-stage calls.

Primary outcomes and inference. Condition-level acceptance: Baseline accepted 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded accepted 141/141 (100.0%). The paired contingency counts are n11 = 135, n10 = 6 (guarded accepted, baseline rejected), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125. The paired absolute estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. All principal numbers derive from archived execution and analysis artifacts.

Discordant-case diagnostics. The six discordant (n10) paired units are traceable to permitted repair-stage activity or sanitizer normalization: in these cases the shared initial draft would have been rejected by the validator but the guarded pipeline (sanitizer and/or a single permitted repair) produced a candidate the validator accepted. The observed increase in guarded acceptance therefore stems from sanitizer normalization and bounded automated repair converting initially invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates rather than from baseline drafts becoming safer prior to generation.

Missingness sensitivity. Nine paired units were excluded because both runs failed technically. Under a conservative sensitivity (treat excluded pairs as failures), baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400; the direction of the observed paired difference remains the same under this conservative accounting. The technical failures reduce effective sample size but do not reverse the observed guarded advantage under these conservative assumptions.

Unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed. As a consequence, this run does not provide empirical estimates of false-positive blocking on benign intents; statements about false-positive rates are therefore omitted and the absence is emphasized here because it constrains operational interpretation.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and limits of the formal estimand. The preregistration's natural-language H1 expected verifier-gating to reduce attacker success; the registered formal estimand measured validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). The observed guarded→higher acceptance (≈4.255 percentage points) occurred because sanitizer and bounded repair recovered reparable drafts the baseline validator rejected. Therefore an increase in validator acceptance does not imply a reduction in attacker success under an attacker-centric definition; acceptance can reflect beneficial repair of benign drafts or, potentially, masking of adversarial manipulation. Distinguishing these alternatives requires an independent semantic-safety oracle not present in the current run.

Operational implications. Within the synthetic setting, sanitizer + bounded repair reduced operator rework by converting invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates. This operational benefit depends on (a) the validator's semantic coverage, (b) the clarity of verifier diagnostics used to guide repairs, and (c) tight limits on repair scope to avoid uncontrolled edits. Deployments should co-design gating policies, repair permissions, and verifier expressiveness to balance automation gains against the risk of masking adversarial manipulations.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: technical failures (18/300) reduced effective N and triggered preregistered exclusions. Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes CLI grammar, sequencing, and protected-interface invariants but omits some protocol-level or dynamic properties; validator acceptance is therefore a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single-model (gpt-5-mini), single-validator, and synthetic-task scope limit generalization across vendors, CLI dialects, and production conditions. Conclusion validity: a ceiling effect (high baseline acceptance) makes absolute gains small; statistically detectable differences can be practically modest. Importantly, the preregistered benign-control and false-positive secondary estimand were not executed, limiting assessment of blocked benign intents.

Recommendations. To improve operational assessment: (1) execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking; (2) preregister an attacker-centric estimand that couples validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle or reachability tests; (3) diversify generators and validators to increase external validity; (4) fix sampling parameters (e.g., set temperature explicitly) for deterministic reproduction.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating with at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostics show the discordant cases were associated with permitted repair or sanitizer normalization enabling acceptance. This formal-estimand improvement does not by itself demonstrate reduced attacker success; distinguishing repair-of-benign-drafts from masking of adversarial manipulations requires an independent semantic-safety oracle and the preregistered benign-control, which was not executed here. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and an unset runtime sampling parameter. Future work should execute the withheld benign-control, broaden models/validators, and pair validator acceptance with independent semantic-safety measurements. All principal numbers and reconciliations reported are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, study selection, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes. Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature; this is disclosed because provider-side defaults can affect sampling determinism. To enable artifact-based verification, the execution and analysis artifacts (execution manifest and analysis results) are archived; these artifacts contain the detailed per-episode traces and provider-call accounting. No human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to deterministic mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
